result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Answer A correctly says the stat columns won't line up because the digits are proportional, recommends tabular-nums, and gives the right eyebrow fix. Its only slips are an optional nudge of the headline line-height to 1.1 and a line-length finding that pushes it to five items. Answer B misreads the stat alignment problem: it says tabular-nums only matters if the values change, and it switches the stats to left alignment. B also includes a typeface finding that it admits is a judgment call rather than a real problem. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B clearly diagnoses the proportional-figure problem in the stacked, right-aligned stats and prescribes tabular-nums. It also states plainly what already works and stays within five non-preference findings. A adds tabular-nums only in passing with a weaker reason and includes a typeface finding that is pure preference. B loses a little for the optional nudge of the headline line-height to 1.1 and for flagging body line length.
